depth_targets.title: Console sign-in (password)
limitations: Vyomi stores a login profile (password-set flag, password-reset-required flag) for an IAM user, but there is no console sign-in flow in this environment to authenticate against it.

depth_targets.title: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices
limitations: Assigning, resyncing or removing a virtual/hardware MFA device is not modeled; no MFA state exists to check at sign-in or policy-condition time.

depth_targets.title: API keys, SSH keys, Git credentials, X.509 certificates
limitations: AWS CodeCommit, Amazon Keyspaces and X.509 signing certificates are not simulated by Vyomi, so the credentials IAM issues for them have nothing to authenticate against.

depth_targets.title: Permissions boundaries
limitations: A permissions boundary ARN is stored on the user/role and reflected in ListEntitiesForPolicy, but Vyomi does not clip the effective permissions to it — SimulatePrincipalPolicy and policy enforcement ignore the boundary.

depth_targets.title: Cross-service authorization enforcement
limitations: IAM policies are stored and evaluated faithfully by SimulatePrincipalPolicy / the Policy simulator page, but Vyomi does not gate other services' native API calls on them: an action an IAM policy would deny still succeeds against S3, DynamoDB, etc. in this environment.

depth_targets.title: Credentials report
limitations: The report is generated synchronously from current user/key state. Fields Vyomi does not track over time — password/key last-used dates, MFA activity — are reported as N/A or false rather than measured.

depth_targets.title: Last Accessed (service last-accessed data)
limitations: Service last-accessed data requires long-term usage telemetry AWS aggregates in the background; Vyomi has no equivalent history to report.

depth_targets.title: Generate policy based on CloudTrail events
limitations: Vyomi does not simulate CloudTrail, so there are no recorded events to mine a least-privilege policy from.

depth_targets.title: IAM Roles Anywhere
limitations: Issuing short-term role credentials to on-premises/X.509-authenticated workloads is not modeled.

depth_targets.title: IAM Access Analyzer
limitations: Resource analysis, unused-access findings and analyzer settings require cross-account reachability analysis Vyomi (a single-account appliance) has no basis to compute.

depth_targets.title: AWS Organizations multi-account features (root access management, organization activity, account access manager)
limitations: Vyomi simulates a single AWS account; there is no organization of member accounts for these multi-account features to operate over.

depth_targets.title: Service control policies (SCPs) and resource control policies (RCPs)
limitations: Vyomi stores and returns SCP/RCP documents (create, list, describe, delete) on IAM's native wire — real AWS routes these through a separate Organizations service.
Vyomi simulates a single AWS account, so attachment to organizational units/accounts and cross-account enforcement are not modeled; policies are validated as JSON but not evaluated.

depth_targets.title: Temporary delegation requests (centralized root access)
limitations: Vyomi has no member accounts to originate a real cross-account access request; this stores and lists request records created over the native wire, with no approval workflow.
